Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase. The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of India A. It will be Narayan Jagadeesan to keep wickets for India A. Khaleel Ahmed has been handed the new ball. It will be the pairing of Andries Gous and Monank Patel to open the innings for the USA. Let's play...
…THE RUN CHASE…

USA face uphill task - Chasing a challenging target of 239, the USA will need a strong and disciplined batting effort to stay in the contest. Can they rise to the occasion, or will the India A bowlers run through the lineup? We’ll find out shortly. Join us soon for the second essay.

Bowlers toil in tough outing -  It was a difficult day in the field for the USA, with most of their bowlers struggling to find rhythm and wickets proving hard to come by. Ali Khan, Jasdeep Singh, and Shubham Ranjane picked up a wicket apiece, with Ranjane standing out as the most impressive. Saurabh Netravalkar also bowled a tidy spell, doing well to keep the scoring in check.

Batting Carnage from India A - A dominant batting performance from India A powered them to a mammoth 238/3 in their 20 overs. Sent in to bat, Priyansh Arya provided a brisk start before falling for 28. Tilak Varma then joined Jagadeesan at the crease, and the pair stitched together a rapid 113-run stand in just over nine overs to lay a solid foundation. Varma departed for 38, but Jagadeesan carried on in style, compiling a superb 104 off just 55 balls, peppering the boundary all around the park. Skipper Ayush Badoni then took charge at the death, smashing an unbeaten 60 off only 26 deliveries to apply the finishing touches and propel the total well past the 230 mark.

A perfect wide yorker to end proceedings but overall, India A had an outstanding outing with the bat. Full and just angled across off, right in the blockhole. Badoni tries to back away but fails to lay a bat on it. India A finish with 238/3 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of USA. It will be the duo of Priyansh Arya and Narayan Jagadeesan who will open the batting for India A. Saurabh Netravalkar will start proceedings with the ball for USA. Let's go...

USA - Ali Khan, Andries Gous, Harmeet Singh, Jasdeep Singh, Milind Kumar, Mohammad Mohsin, Monank Patel, Nosthush Kenjige, Saiteja Mukkamalla, Sanjay Krishnamurthi, Saurabh Netravalkar, Shadley van Schalkwyk, Shayan Jahangir, Shehan Jayasuriya, and Shubham Ranjane.

India A - Ashok Sharma, Ashutosh Sharma, Ayush Badoni (C), Gurjapneet Singh, Khaleel Ahmed, Manav Suthar, Mayank Yadav, Naman Dhir, Narayan Jagadeesan, Priyansh Arya, Ravi Bishnoi, Riyan Parag, Tilak Varma, Urvil Patel, and Vipraj Nigam.
TOSS - USA win the toss and elected to BOWL first.

A welcome challenge for India A - As for India A, this presents a strong opportunity to test themselves against World Cup-bound oppositions, with another fixture against Namibia lined up next. The squad features quality domestic talent who have impressed in the IPL and on the domestic circuit. The batting is led by Riyan Parag, Ayush Badoni, Naman Dhir and Ashutosh Sharma. The pace attack includes Khaleel Ahmed, Gurjapneet Singh and Mayank Yadav, while Ravi Bishnoi will spearhead the spin department.

USA carry confidence from 2024 - USA enjoyed a memorable T20 World Cup debut in 2024, reaching the Super 8 stage, with their Super Over win against Pakistan the standout moment of the campaign. Monank Patel leads the side once again, with much of the core retained from that squad. The batting will revolve around Monank Patel, Andries Gous and Shayan Jahangir. Left-arm seamer Saurabh Netravalkar was a standout in the previous edition and will partner Ali Khan, while spin duties fall to Harmeet Singh and Nosthush Kenjige.

Final preparations - With less than a week to go for the World Cup, teams dive into their warm-up games to put the finishing touches on their preparations. In match number two, the United States take on India A at the Dr DY Patil Sports Academy in Navi Mumbai.
